title: Reading a joint distribution

prereqs.why: The table is a joint distribution and the question is about reading one.
The answer is a conditional, obtained from the joint and a marginal.
Checking whether the table factorises is the natural follow-up.

statement:
Two random variables $X$ and $Y$ each take the values $0$ and $1$, with this joint distribution:

| $\P(X=x, Y=y)$ | $y = 0$ | $y = 1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x = 0$ | $1/4$ | $1/8$ |
| $x = 1$ | $1/8$ | $1/2$ |

Compute $\P(X = 1 \mid Y = 1)$, exactly.
hints: A conditional comes from a joint divided by a marginal: $\P(X=1 \mid Y=1) = \P(X=1, Y=1) / \P(Y=1)$.
The marginal $\P(Y=1)$ is the sum of the $y=1$ **column** — both ways $Y$ can equal $1$.

payload.label: Probability
payload.syntax: A fraction or an expression. (1/2)/(5/8) is read and worked out exactly.
